Subject: Pre-Procurement: Certification requests & supplier onboarding checklist (Storica)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for moving quickly on the evaluation. Procurement at Redwood needs the following items to complete supplier setup so we can issue PO-2093 and enable billing:

1) Certificates of Insurance (COI) for:
   - General Liability (GL): $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate, Redwood Inference listed as certificate holder (address below).
   - Professional Liability / E&O: $1M per claim, claims-made or occurrence acceptable (please note retroactive date if claims-made).
   - Cyber Liability: $1M minimum; privacy / breach coverage called out.

2) W-9 or equivalent tax form (if US entity).
3) Signed vendor onboarding form (I've attached the checklist template).
4) Expected remit-to / invoice email and a copy of your standard invoice.

If you can provide the COIs and W-9 by close of business Wednesday (06/24) we can route PO-2093 within two business days. If any of the policy limits can't be met, flag exceptions and provide an attestation letter from your broker and an expected date for updated coverage.

Certificate holder (please mirror exactly on COI):
Redwood Inference, Inc.
330 Montgomery St, Suite 100
San Francisco, CA 94104

I've included Monica to coordinate PO details and Laura for vendor onboarding and legal redlines.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Storica live.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Vivek —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick update from our side: we can deliver the GL and E&O COIs with the requested limits, and our broker is finalizing the cyber endorsement to explicitly include privacy/breach coverage. We expect all documents by EOD Wednesday (06/24).

Two small notes:
- Our E&O is a claims-made policy with a retroactive date of 2019-05-01 — will that be acceptable?
- For the COI holder address, we can add Redwood as the certificate holder and include the policy number, but the broker historically redacts full policy limits on cyber. We can provide an attestation letter from the broker confirming limits and effective dates if necessary.

I've looped Emily from RiskDocs — she will upload the COIs and the broker attestation to your Drive link once received.

Thanks Jordan —

Claims-made E&O with a 2019 retroactive date is acceptable provided the carrier confirms the retro date on the COI. For cyber redactions: an attestation letter plus the COI stub (showing carrier name, policy number, and limits even if specific settlements are redacted) is usually fine for our risk team. Please ensure the COI names Redwood Inference exactly as the certificate holder.

Action items on our side:
- I'll generate PO-2093 (draft) and route it to procurement@storica.com after we have the COIs and W-9.
- Laura, can you confirm whether we need a separate vendor security questionnaire completed for Storica or if acceptable to rely on the COIs + existing SOC2 reference?

Jordan — please include remit-to address for invoices (email + postal if necessary) and whether you require the PO number on the invoice PDF. If you can confirm those two items in your COI upload it will speed approval.

Monica Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142
